housing.summary: Zurich is Switzerland's most expensive rental market. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 2,519/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

banking.summary: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents typically need a valid passport or national ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and sometimes a work permit or residence permit. UBS and Zürcher Kantonalbank (ZKB) are the main banks in Zurich. PostFinance is a nationwide option. Online account opening available at most banks.
required_docs: Employer letter or salary slip (sometimes required)

schools.summary: Zurich hosts numerous international schools offering IB, British, American and other curricula, including the International School of Zurich North, Zurich International School (ZIS), and Inter-Community School (ICS). The Swiss federation of international schools maintains a directory.

legal_admin.summary: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle (residents' registration office) of their municipality within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for a permit B (over 1 year) or L (under 1 year) at the Cantonal Migration Office. Non-EU nationals need a residence permit from the cantonal authority (Migrationsamt Zürich) before or upon arrival. Authority: sem.admin.ch.
legal_admin.registration_step: Anmeldung at Einwohnerkontrolle within 14 days; residence permit from cantonal migration authority

tax_finance.summary: Every employed or self-employed person in Switzerland receives an AHV-Nummer (OASI/AHV social security number), which also serves as the Swiss tax ID. It is assigned by the cantonal AHV compensation office or the employer upon commencement of employment. Zurich's cantonal authority is the SVA Zürich (svazurich.ch). The number is 13 digits (756.XXXX.XXXX.XX).

transport.summary: Zurich's public transport is operated by ZVV (Zürcher Verkehrsverbund), encompassing trams, buses, S-Bahn, and boats. A monthly zone pass (zones 110+121, city area) costs approximately CHF 88 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences can be exchanged at the Strassenverkehrsamt Zürich within 12 months of establishing residency without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung (basic health insurance) must be taken out within 3 months of arrival or gaining residency; regulated by the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG/OFSP) at bag.admin.ch.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EFTA licences exchangeable within 12 months at Strassenverkehrsamt Zürich (mfz.zh.ch); non-EU licences require a theory and practical test
transport.healthcare_registration: Mandatory basic health insurance (Krankenversicherung/KVG) must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; choose a licensed insurer at bag.admin.ch
